Counts below are completed finite checks, not a claim that the long cohorts have finished.\n\n') if a.preview else ''
text=intro+'''Visual resets, recording and offline batches made avoidable copies or Python allocations; large numeric checks allocated image-sized scratch. Interrupted cleanup could retain sockets/listeners/children or hide the original error. This PR reduces measured CPU work/allocation, hardens recoverable PPO and preserves owned arrays, terminal observations and episode boundaries.

- Add versioned policy/Adam recovery points, verified resume reads and bounded log-std endpoint gradients.
- Add compact episodes, bounded background writers, projected/sharded readers and owned streaming batches; reduce recorder/reset work and shuffled-batch validation overhead.
- Keep full-range integer episode/step identities exact in executors, recording and readers; reject malformed/nonrepresentable JSON identity markers and stale action reuse at maximum-step wrap.
- Complete interrupted Web/Wuji/Go1/renderer cleanup, preserving primary errors and releasing worker/socket/pipe handles; restore original or nested Go1 hooks.
- Limit sparse Go1 reset/motion gathers and large validation/hashing scratch; correct Microduck anatomical head CoM selection and expand CPU/native/browser/installed-wheel coverage.

Current source `49079dd`: **1,603 passed** on Python 3.10 (95 optional skips), **1,665 passed** on Python 3.12 + mjbatch (84 skips). NumPy1.24 targeted checks passed 324; the overlapping native/live/Web/data subset passed 385 (one skip). Ruff checked 208 files. A new isolated Python3.10/NumPy1.24 installation matched all 153 packaged files and passed 242 tests without Torch/MuJoCo or checkout imports. Six actual Go1 live cases per source executed 240 control steps with exact state hashes and reaped workers through injected wait interruptions, using a seeded untrained policy. Forty isolated real-signal wait interruptions also reaped every child/socket/private directory; two old-source controls failed as expected. SIGTERM in that harness uses a SystemExit handler, not the production default signal behavior.

The latest shuffled offline read/decode/validation/batch benchmark shows **8.49–13.71% lower median time** across four synthetic state-data configurations in 20 alternating subprocess pairs; initial eight-pair results were 10.8–17.1% lower. Output and instruction hashes match. Complete traced peaks are essentially unchanged. One unchanged ordered control was 10.58% slower in the subprocess confirmation; warm same-process follow-up put ordered cases within about -0.6% to +0.12% time change, while shuffled cases were 12.1–13.5% lower. Both results and all paired observations are retained. No ordered-path or whole-training speedup is claimed.

Direct large-body JSON receive is faster in the 0.25–4MB synthetic cases (about 10–20% lower time across the two measurement settings), with essentially unchanged complete decode peaks. Actual Go1 states were roughly 0.7–38KB and showed no stable benefit; they stay below the 64KiB product threshold. The 16KiB experiment was rejected. Small-message noise/regressions remain visible. Shared-host pinning does not reserve a CPU, and these timings are not RSS bounds, statistical guarantees or online-control gains.

Earlier scoped improvements retain their original baselines: round6 N16/S540 local contiguous depth-validation scratch fell from about 9.34MB to 0.53MB, but **complete visual-reset peak and large full-reset median times stayed essentially unchanged**. Small local N1/S128 time increased 3.46%; compatible cached executor peaks stayed unchanged and timing series included 3–12% slower cases. Round5 measured 46.5% lower cached action-call traced peak at N4096/A32 and roughly 3–11% lower recorder append time; large Go1 motion extraction used 1,496 versus 99,320 traced bytes, while N1 used 416 more bytes. These gains are separate and are not additive training speedups.

Round4's three paired Go1 PPO seeds completed 300 updates (22,118,400 transitions/source), with exact metrics, policy/Adam, RNG and physics-state hashes. Microduck quality remains mixed after the anatomical change to its MDP/reset distribution: survival at 1,000 updates was 935/960 versus 951/960, and at 2,500 total updates 945/960 versus 948/960. Seed0 tracking worsened; seed2 tracking improved while survival fell to 313/320 versus 319/320. There is no universal, mature-policy or real-robot quality claim. Checkpoint/curriculum identities were audited; simulation/RNG restart semantics remain explicit.

'''
